manifest.name: afc-lite
manifest.title: AFC Lite (Automated Filament Changer)
manifest.description: Lightweight Automated Filament Changer support for the Snapmaker U1's four toolheads. Ships the AFC, AFC_unit and AFC_lane Klipper extras plus an afc.cfg that maps the four lanes (E0-E3) to the U1 extruders and filament motion sensors, and adds gcode macros for color, material, vendor, map, spool id, weight, tool change and lane/tool unload. Per-lane state feeds the U1's SET_PRINT_FILAMENT_CONFIG so the slicer and screen track what is loaded.
manifest.tagline: Four-lane filament tracking and tool-change macros for the U1.

manifest.name: camera-hw-accel
manifest.title: Camera HW Accel
manifest.description:
Tap into the SoC's video pipeline instead of CPU-encoding every frame. MJPEG over HTTP at /webcam, WebRTC at /webrtc; works on any browser, smooth 30fps even with two cameras attached.

To have these auto-registered as cameras in Fluidd and Mainsail (so you don't have to add them by hand under Settings → Cameras), also install b3d://bespok3d-org/webcam-builtin for the built-in MIPI camera and b3d://bespok3d-org/webcam-usb for the external USB camera.
manifest.tagline: HW-accelerated MJPEG and WebRTC streaming for MIPI & USB cameras.

config.label: WebRTC stream
config.hint: On by default: the Fluidd/Mainsail camera tile is registered for the WebRTC stream. Turning it off saves memory, but ONLY do so if your camera is set to the MJPEG stream, otherwise the tile goes blank.

config.label: Built-in camera resolution
config.hint: Capture resolution for the built-in (MIPI) camera. 720p uses less memory and CPU, handy on low-RAM boards. The external USB camera always uses its own native resolution.

config.label: Recycle WebRTC viewers after (minutes, 0 = off)
config.hint: 0 (recommended): a camera stays connected as long as you watch it. Set a number of minutes to periodically recycle each WebRTC viewer connection as a memory-safety backstop on a very constrained board; the tile reconnects on its own within a couple of seconds, so it no longer freezes. Dead or abandoned viewers are always cleaned up regardless of this setting.

manifest.name: idle-timeout
manifest.title: Idle Timeout
manifest.description: Sets how long the printer waits, with no activity, before it powers down its motors and heaters (Klipper's idle timeout). The Snapmaker U1 ships with a short 5 minute (300 second) timeout, which can cut power mid-workflow while you swap filament or level by hand. Set the timeout you want, in seconds; the plugin overrides the printer's idle_timeout value so it sticks across prints. Default is 7200 seconds (2 hours).
manifest.tagline: Choose how long the printer stays awake before it powers its motors down.

variables.name: IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
variables.description: Idle timeout in seconds (a positive whole number). 3600 = 1 hour, 7200 = 2 hours.

config.label: Idle timeout (seconds)
config.hint: Seconds of inactivity before the printer powers its motors and heaters down. 3600 = 1 hour, 7200 = 2 hours. Must be a positive whole number.

manifest.tagline: Mainsail web interface alongside Fluidd, on your chosen port.

manifest.name: moonraker-notify
manifest.title: Print Notifications
manifest.description: Sends a push notification when a print finishes, fails, or errors, using Moonraker's [notifier] and the Apprise library. Apprise speaks to about a hundred services from one address: Telegram, Discord, Slack, ntfy, Pushover, email, Matrix, Home Assistant, and more. Paste the Apprise URL for your service (e.g. ntfy://ntfy.sh/your-topic or tgram://bottoken/chatid) and pick which events to be told about. The Apprise library is baked into the package and linked into Moonraker's interpreter at install; no pip ever runs on the printer.
manifest.tagline: Get a ping on your phone or chat when a print finishes or fails.

variables.name: APPRISE_URL
variables.description: Apprise URL for your notification service (e.g. ntfy://ntfy.sh/your-topic)

config.label: Notifier name
config.hint: A label for this destination; you can install more than one.

config.label: Apprise URL
config.hint: Your service's Apprise URL. See github.com/caronc/apprise for the format per service.

config.label: Notify on
config.hint: Which print events trigger a notification.

manifest.name: remote-screen
manifest.title: Remote Screen
manifest.description:
Mirror the printer's on-device touchscreen to a browser. Low-overhead framebuffer capture, no UI changes on the device side.

To have the screen appear as a tile in Fluidd and Mainsail (alongside your cameras, no manual setup under Settings → Cameras), also install b3d://bespok3d-org/webcam-screen; registers the mirror as a Moonraker [webcam] iframe entry sized for the U1's 480:320 display.
manifest.tagline: Stream your printer's framebuffer as MJPEG.

manifest.name: rfid-anycubic
manifest.title: Anycubic ACE Filament Tag
manifest.description: Reads Anycubic ACE filament tags (plaintext NTAG21x, no key) and decodes the dispute-free fields - brand, material, and nozzle/bed temperatures - into the shared rfid_data.json. PARTIAL by design: the public reverse engineering disagrees on three fields (the SKU length, the color byte order, and whether page 31 is weight), and no real tag dump has been published to settle them, so this decoder does NOT decode color, diameter, or weight yet rather than guess. One captured tag from a tester pins those, then they are added. Installs the RFID Spool Reader automatically. Read-only. Experiment channel.
manifest.tagline: Decode Anycubic ACE brand/material/temps (color+weight pending a tag dump).

manifest.name: rfid-bambu
manifest.title: Bambu Filament Tag
manifest.description: Reads Bambu Lab filament spool tags (encrypted Mifare Classic) and decodes the full filament: material, color, diameter, weight, and nozzle/bed temperatures into the shared rfid_data.json. REQUIRES A KEY YOU SUPPLY: Bambu tags are encrypted, so you must paste the public Bambu master key into this plugin's config (see the documentation for where to get it) before the tag can be decoded. Without a key the spool is still tracked by its tag UID. Installs the RFID Spool Reader automatically. Read-only: it never writes a tag. Experiment channel until verified on a real tag.
manifest.tagline: Decode Bambu spools on stock firmware (you supply the key).

config.label: Bambu master key (hex)
config.hint: The public Bambu master key. You paste it; we never ship it. See the plugin documentation for where to get it. Leave empty to track Bambu spools by UID only (no decode).

manifest.name: rfid-creality
manifest.title: Creality Filament Tag
manifest.description: Reads Creality CFS filament spool tags (encrypted Mifare Classic) and decodes the filament: color, weight, manufacture date, and material id into the shared rfid_data.json. REQUIRES TWO KEYS YOU SUPPLY: Creality tags are encrypted, so you must paste the public Creality master key and payload key into this plugin's config (see the documentation for where to get them) before a tag can be decoded. Without the keys the spool is still tracked by its tag UID. Creality's tag carries no diameter or temperatures (the printer resolves those from an unpublished material database), and the material id stays a numeric id. Installs the RFID Spool Reader automatically. Read-only: it never writes a tag. Experiment channel until verified on a real tag.
manifest.tagline: Decode Creality CFS spools on stock firmware (you supply the keys).

config.label: Creality master key (hex)
config.hint: The public Creality master key (derives the card key from the tag UID). You paste it; we never ship it. See the plugin documentation. Leave empty to track Creality spools by UID only (no decode).

config.label: Creality payload key (hex)
config.hint: The public Creality payload key (decrypts the filament block). You paste it; we never ship it. See the plugin documentation. Both keys are needed to decode; leave empty for UID-only tracking.

manifest.name: rfid-elegoo
manifest.title: Elegoo Filament Tag
manifest.description: EXPERIMENTAL. Decoder for Elegoo's published NTAG EPC-256 tag layout (material, color, diameter, weight), anchored on Elegoo's manufacturer signature in the raw page dump. IMPORTANT (verified on a real U1, 2026-06-29): the FACTORY Elegoo Centauri spool tags do NOT read on the U1 today. The cause is the U1 reader's antenna coupling with that specific tag, not this decoder and not a locked tag: the data is open NTAG213 memory, but the reader gets no RF wake-up response from the factory tag, across the entire register space and both coils, while M1/NTAG read fine and phones/Canvas read the Elegoo. The decoder is correct and ready for any Elegoo tag presenting the published layout (or the day the reader can wake the factory tag). Workaround: an OpenSpool NTAG on the opposite side of the spool ring. See the doc for full findings + a community call to action. Requires the RFID Spool Reader. Read-only.
manifest.tagline: Elegoo NTAG EPC-256 decoder (factory U1 tags blocked by reader RF, see doc).

manifest.name: rfid-generic-ndef
manifest.title: Generic NDEF Filament Tag
manifest.description: Best-effort reader for filament NFC tags that store their data as plain JSON in an NDEF record but do not use a recognized protocol (OpenSpool and other protocol-keyed tags are handled by their own decoders). Maps common field names (brand, type, color_hex, min_temp/max_temp, bed_temp, diameter, weight) into the shared rfid_data.json. Requires the RFID Spool Reader, which it installs automatically. Read-only: it never writes a tag. Experiment channel until verified on a real tag.
manifest.tagline: Read any plain-JSON NFC filament tag the U1 reader can see.

manifest.name: rfid-ntag
manifest.title: RFID Spool Reader
manifest.description: USB RFID reader picks up OpenSpool-encoded NTAG215 cards. Writes the current spool's metadata to rfid_data.json on every card event so the rest of the stack just knows.
manifest.tagline: NTAG215/OpenSpool RFID: your filament knows what it is.

conflict_resolutions.description: FW <=1.4.0.38 uses ppins GPIO (not gpiod); different patch context required for fm175xx_reader.py
FW <=1.4.0.38 uses copy.deepcopy; different patch context required for filament_detect.py

manifest.name: rfid-openprinttag
manifest.title: OpenPrintTag Filament Tag
manifest.description: Decodes the OpenPrintTag (prusa3d) filament data format - an open CBOR payload - off any NTAG21x the reader can read, mapping material, brand, color, diameter, weight, manufacture date, and nozzle/bed/drying temperatures into the shared rfid_data.json. No key required. Note: Prusa's own factory spools use ISO-15693 tags the U1 reader cannot read; this targets OpenPrintTag payloads written onto a standard NTAG21x. Installs the RFID Spool Reader automatically. Read-only. Experiment channel until verified on a real tag.
manifest.tagline: Decode the OpenPrintTag data format on NTAG (no key).

manifest.name: rfid-opentag
manifest.title: OpenTag3D Filament Tag
manifest.description: Reads OpenTag3D (queengooborg open standard) filament NFC tags: the big-endian binary payload carried in an NDEF application/opentag3d record (manufacturer, material, color, diameter, weight, nozzle and bed temperatures) is decoded into the shared rfid_data.json. Plaintext, no key needed. Requires the RFID Spool Reader, which it installs automatically. Read-only: it never writes a tag. Experiment channel until verified on a real tag.
manifest.tagline: Read OpenTag3D open-standard filament tags on stock firmware.

manifest.name: rfid-tigertag
manifest.title: TigerTag Filament Tag
manifest.description: Reads TigerTag filament tags (open NTAG21x, no key required) and decodes the physical filament data - color (RGBA), diameter, nozzle and bed temperatures, drying temperature, and weight - into the shared rfid_data.json. The brand and material are stored on a TigerTag as numeric ids whose human-name tables are GPLv3, so this decoder keeps them as ids rather than vendoring a GPL table; the product id is surfaced as the SKU. Works on the standard NTAG reader (no key, no reader change). Installs the RFID Spool Reader automatically. Read-only. Experiment channel until verified on a real tag.
manifest.tagline: Decode open TigerTag NTAG spools (color, temps, diameter, weight).

manifest.name: spoolman
manifest.title: Spoolman Bridge
manifest.description: Spoolman for the U1 multi-tool: the active spool follows the tag the printer reads or the spool you pick, color and material reach the screen and AFC panel, tags are matched by their hardware UID, and you can record which printer each spool is on. Filament length per print is logged automatically.
manifest.tagline: Zero-config Spoolman: active spool always tracked.

macros.name: SET_ACTIVE_SPOOL
macros.description: Set the selected tool as the active spool.

macros.name: CLEAR_ALL_SPOOLS
macros.description: Clear the selected spool for every tool.

macros.name: DETECT_SPOOLS
macros.description: Re-detect the loaded spools. A handy reset when spool state looks wrong.

macros.name: DUMP_SPOOLS
macros.description: Print what the bridge knows about the loaded spools.

macros.name: READ_FILAMENT_ID
macros.description: Read the selected lane's spool tag, if any.

macros.name: GET_FILAMENT_ID
macros.description: Print the currently read tag for the selected lane.

macros.name: SH_BIND_CARD_UID
macros.description: Bind the tag UID currently on a lane to a Spoolman spool, so the next tap of that tag resolves to it directly.

macros.name: SH_CONFIG
macros.description: Change mode and logging at runtime, no restart.

macros.name: SH_DEBUG
macros.description: Print the current configuration; with a SKU, show the spool it would track.

variables.name: SPOOLMAN_SERVER
variables.description: Spoolman server address with port, e.g. 192.168.1.50:8000

variables.name: SPOOLMAN_MODE
variables.description: How the active spool is chosen: auto (RFID first) or manual.

variables.name: SPOOLMAN_LOGGING
variables.description: Log verbosity: error, info, warn, verbose, or debug.

variables.name: SPOOLMAN_TRACK_LOCATION
variables.description: Write this printer's name into a loaded spool's Spoolman location, and clear it on unload.

variables.name: SPOOLMAN_LOCATION
variables.description: This printer's name, written to a loaded spool's Spoolman location field.

config.label: Spoolman server address
config.hint: Host or host:port of your Spoolman instance.

config.label: Selection mode
config.hint: auto: RFID is the source of truth, falls back to the manual spool. manual: the manual selection drives, tags are the fallback.

config.label: Log level
config.hint: How chatty the logs are, from least to most.

config.label: Spool resolution order
config.hint: Comma-separated, first match wins. Options: spool_id (id on the tag), uid (the tag's hardware UID, bound in Spoolman), sku.

config.label: Auto-bind tag UID on SKU match
config.hint: Opt-in (off by default). When on, a spool found by SKU that has no UID yet gets the current tag's UID written onto it in Spoolman, so the next tap is a direct UID match. Off means tags are only ever bound on your explicit request (SH_BIND_CARD_UID).

config.label: Track spool location in Spoolman
config.hint: When on, a spool loaded on this printer gets this printer's name written to its Spoolman location, and it is cleared when the spool is unloaded -- so you can see in Spoolman which printer a spool is on.

config.label: This printer's name (Spoolman location)
config.hint: The name written as a loaded spool's location in Spoolman (e.g. unU1jr). Location tracking is inactive until a name is set.

manifest.name: status-feed
manifest.title: Status Feed
manifest.description:
A small sidecar that serves a human-readable print-status summary as JSON at /status-feed/. It runs as its own Python service in a per-plugin virtual environment, so its one dependency (humanize) is fully isolated from the system, Klipper, and Moonraker interpreters.

This is the reference plugin for the declarative Python-dependency mechanism (ADR-0036): the manifest declares its dependency as data and the daemon provisions and tears down the venv.
manifest.tagline: Human-readable printer status as a JSON feed.

manifest.name: tailscale
manifest.title: Tailscale
manifest.description: Joins the printer to your Tailscale mesh network (tailnet), so you can reach Fluidd/Mainsail, the camera, and SSH from anywhere without opening a port on your router. Bring your own account: generate an auth key at login.tailscale.com/admin/settings/keys, then paste it below. The printer authorizes itself the way any Tailscale device does; it appears in your tailnet's device list like a laptop or phone. Bespok3d hosts no coordination service and never sees your auth key or traffic. Runs tailscaled as a managed service on top of the tun-module base (a real /dev/net/tun the tailscale0 network interface needs).
manifest.tagline: Reach your printer from anywhere over your Tailscale network.

variables.name: TS_AUTHKEY
variables.description: An auth key from your tailnet's admin console (login.tailscale.com/admin/settings/keys), starting with tskey-auth-.

config.label: Tailscale auth key
config.hint: From your tailnet's admin console (login.tailscale.com/admin/settings/keys, then Generate auth key; a brand-new account lands on an 'add a device' wizard first, open the keys page directly). Turn on Reusable: a reusable key lets you reinstall without generating a new one, and one reusable key can join several printers (each appears as its own device). Bring your own account; Bespok3d hosts nothing.

manifest.name: tun-module
manifest.title: TUN kernel module
manifest.description: Loads the Linux `tun` kernel module so the printer has a working /dev/net/tun. Mesh-VPN plugins (ZeroTier needs it; Tailscale runs lighter with it) build a virtual network interface on top of it. The Snapmaker U1's stock kernel ships tun neither built in nor as a module, so this plugin carries a `tun.ko` cross-built against the exact running kernel (6.1.99 aarch64) and insmods it at boot, before the services that need it. Nothing to configure: install it (or install a VPN plugin that requires it) and /dev/net/tun is there.
manifest.tagline: Adds /dev/net/tun to the printer, the base a mesh VPN builds on.

manifest.name: u1-gcode-colors
manifest.title: U1 G-code Preview Colors
manifest.description: Fills Fluidd's G-code preview filament_colors array from the U1's live print_task state, so each tool line shows the color actually loaded on the extruder it maps to, instead of the fixed fallback palette. No Fluidd patch. Works with any color source the printer already has (RFID, screen picks, or the Spoolman helper if installed).
manifest.tagline: Real per-tool colors in the G-code preview, from what is actually loaded.

variables.name: GCODE_COLORS_ENABLED
variables.description: Whether the G-code preview fill runs (true) or leaves Fluidd on its fallback palette (false)

config.label: Fill real per-tool colors
config.hint: On: the G-code preview shows each tool's actually loaded color. Off: Fluidd falls back to its default palette.

manifest.name: zerotier
manifest.title: ZeroTier
manifest.description: Joins the printer to a ZeroTier mesh network, so you can reach Fluidd/Mainsail, the camera, and SSH from anywhere without opening a port on your router. Bring your own account: create a free network at my.zerotier.com, then paste its 16-hex-digit network id below. The printer authorizes itself the way any ZeroTier device does; approve it in ZeroTier Central like you would a laptop or phone. Bespok3d hosts no coordination service and never sees your network id or traffic. Runs zerotier-one as a managed service on top of the tun-module base (a real /dev/net/tun the ZeroTier virtual network interface needs).
manifest.tagline: Reach your printer from anywhere over a ZeroTier mesh network.

variables.name: ZT_NETWORK_ID
variables.description: The 16 hex digit ZeroTier network id to join, from your ZeroTier Central account (my.zerotier.com).

config.label: ZeroTier network id
config.hint: 16 hex digits, from your ZeroTier Central account (my.zerotier.com). Bring your own network; Bespok3d hosts nothing. After install, approve the printer's device in ZeroTier Central.
